title: Your Brain, Amplified: Learning in the Age of AI
description:
This session delves into how AI can be a powerful co-pilot in our learning journey, uncovering innovative ways to master new skills and deepen our understanding across various fields.

We'll explore how AI tools can amplify our cognitive abilities and make learning more efficient, personalized, and engaging.

The focus is practical and aimed at students, professionals, lifelong learners, and anyone curious about leveraging AI to accelerate their personal and professional growth – educators and learning designers will also find valuable insights in these discussions.

We'll explore-
\* The current landscape of AI tools designed for learning – beyond simple chatbots, identifying what's truly impactful.
\* Tailoring AI for diverse disciplines – from coding and creative writing to scientific research and language acquisition, adapting to subject-specific needs.
\* Crafting personalized learning paths with AI – adapting to your unique pace, style, and goals to optimize retention and comprehension.
\* Leveraging AI for deep understanding – summarizing complex texts, generating critical questions, identifying knowledge gaps, and exploring different perspectives.
\* Interactive learning with AI – using AI for active recall, spaced repetition, generating practice scenarios, and simulated environments.
\* Avoiding the pitfalls: identifying where AI can hinder genuine learning, encourage shallow engagement, or produce misleading information, and how to maintain intellectual rigor.
\* Building your AI-enhanced learning toolkit – practical workflows and strategies for effective integration into your daily study or work routine.
\* Developing a personal learning strategy – how to thoughtfully combine traditional methods with AI assistance to maximize your learning outcomes.

After the discussion, we often continue the conversation over dinner nearby, a great opportunity to connect with fellow learners and innovators.

description:
Sick of loud bars, awkward small talk, and surface-level chats?
I am too.

Let’s do something low-key - but *real*.

**🌿 Walk & Talk** \- a casual\, open\-invite stroll with people who enjoy movement\, connection\, and actual conversation\.

No agenda, no pressure, and no hierarchies.

The event language is English, but you are welcome to use other languages when chatting with others.

title: Sit & Think: Inaugural Session of a Rhetorical Forum
location: 2 Freyberg Place, Auckland CBD, Auckland 1000, Betty Wark Room, Auckland
description:
This is the first full session of Sit & Think, a new civil community forum inspired by the spirit of free exchange of ideas at Walk & Talk meetups. The session features a short talk on a theme from politics, philosophy, or public life, followed by a hands-on exercise and an open, facilitated discussion. Sit & Think is hosted by Dr Dmitry Zavialov.

The inaugural session, presented by Walk & Talk Auckland in partnership with the Ellen Melville Centre, introduces a practical toolkit for reading rhetoric: how to spot when a message appeals to your reason, your emotions, or your trust in authority, and how to tell the difference between persuasion and manipulation. The tools we practise in this session are the same ones we will use to hold ourselves to a higher standard of conversation in every session that follows.

No prior knowledge required. No prep, no reading. Just bring your curiosity and your willingness to think. Places are limited; make sure to RSVP.

**How the room works**

Disagreement is welcome. Dominance is not. You do not need to agree with anyone, but we ask that you disagree with the idea, not the person; that you listen before you respond; and that you make room for voices other than your own. This is not a debate, and there is no winner. If you tend to speak a lot, practise holding back. If you tend to hold back, this is a room where your voice is wanted. The facilitator will step in if the conversation needs steering. That is the job, not a criticism of anyone.

**📅 When:** Saturday 25 July, 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM
**📍 Where:** Betty Wark Room, Ellen Melville Centre, 2 Freyberg Place, Auckland CBD
**🎙️ Format:** Short talk → group analysis → pair exercise → open discussion
**💵 Cost:** Free. Koha welcome.
**♿ Access:** Ground floor, accessible venue.
Presented by Walk & Talk Auckland in partnership with the Ellen Melville Centre.

title: Build Night: Demos, Collabs & Open Source in Practice
description:
A fortnightly, hands-on session focused on the projects the Auckland AI Collective is actually building — together.

Each session centres on **demonstrations** of what members are working on. Expect live demos, group experiments, and the occasional "let's just try it and see what happens" moment — so come ready to get involved, not just watch. Some parts may invite your participation; none of it is polished or precious.

The tone is **casual and informal**\- eat dinner\, drink\, and enjoy\. This is a place to share ideas\, get feedback\, find collaborators\, and turn "someone should build that" into an actual repo\.

What we cover will vary week to week depending on what people bring and what the group is curious about — the constant is the room: builders comparing notes and starting things together.

**This is for you if** you want to get directly and personally involved in group projects, collaborations, and open source.

See what we're already building on GitHub: [https://github.com/auckland-ai-collective](https://github.com/auckland-ai-collective)

Bring a project, a problem, an idea, or just yourself.

After this session we can hang out as long as we like at the restaurant if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

title: Improverished Open Workshop - July
description:
Kia ora! Welcome!

These workshops are a fun monthly event, open for anyone to come along and do some improv in a low-pressure, friendly environment. Never done improv before? You're welcome to come along and try it out! Done tons of improv before? You're welcome to come along too! Last Saturday of every month. Koha is optional but appreciated. Read on to find out more ![🙂](https://static.xx.fbcdn.net/images/emoji.php/v9/t4c/1/16/1f642.png)

What exactly we cover will depend on who ends up coming along on the day, but you can expect some laughs and a chance to embrace silliness and joyful failure.

There is no set charge to attend. We appreciate a Koha contribution towards our operating costs but you are still always welcome even if you're not in a position to contribute this month.

title: Building Deterministic, Agentic AI
location: Level 19, Vero Centre, 48 Shortland Street, Auckland CBD, Auckland
description:
Hello everyone,

We're excited to invite you to the **Auckland AWS Tools and Programming meetup**!

This month, we are diving deep into the architecture behind moving AI from prototype chatbots to production-grade, deterministic agentic systems. We are thrilled to host **[Sam Low](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sam-l-9b094230/) (Tech Lead @ Pushpay)**!

We are gathering once again at the *Pushpay office in the CBD*—looking forward to seeing you all there!

🚨 **Action Required:** To help us streamline building security and sort out the catering (including dietary requirements), please make sure to pre-register before arriving: 👉 **[Pre-register for Venue Check-In Here](https://eventspaces.app/e/building-deterministic-agentic-ai-architectural-blueprint-for-a-production-grade-langgraph-stack-92edec/register)**

**🎤 The Lineup**
**Sam Low (Tech Lead @ Pushpay)**

**Title:** Building Deterministic, Agentic AI: Architectural Blueprint for a Production-Grade LangGraph Stack

**Description:** Moving AI from a prototype chatbot to a production-ready agent shifts the risk from text-based vulnerabilities to execution-based ones. In a natural language to SQL (NL2SQL) system, a single unvalidated execution can cause a catastrophic data leak, and you cannot prompt-engineer your way out of it.

This session unpacks an architectural blueprint for building deterministic fail-safes around non-deterministic AI models. We will explore the core load-bearing pillars: Context Retrieval, Orchestration, and Evals. We will cover how to utilize LangGraph to enforce immutable state machine boundaries, sanitize execution payloads, and mandate tenant isolation.

Attendees will walk away with a structural design pattern for a secure orchestration engine that retains absolute veto power over the model's imagination.
